args.reply_to_member:
Thank you for reporting this quickly. Because you told us about the lost or stolen card within two business days, your liability for the $400 ATM withdrawal on October 20 is limited to $50. Under the regulation, your liability is the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur before you notified us, so the maximum you would owe is $50.

What happens next: we need to investigate the withdrawal. We must decide within 10 business days of receiving your notice, which is by November 4, 2026. We may take up to 45 days (by December 5, 2026) if we need more time, but if we do, we must provisionally credit your account within 10 business days, and we can withhold no more than $50 of that credit. We must report the results to you within three business days after finishing the investigation.

Please also check your statements. If a periodic statement showing this withdrawal was sent to you, you must report any unauthorized transfers on it within 60 days of when it was sent to avoid unlimited liability for later unauthorized transfers. Since you have already reported the card as stolen, please also make sure any other unauthorized activity is reported to us right away.

This case has been referred to our disputes team for a human review.

args.reply_to_member:
Thank you for reporting these transfers. Here is how the rules apply to your situation.

Your September 30 statement showed the $120 debit from September 20. Under the rules, you had to report an unauthorized transfer that appears on a periodic statement within 60 days after the statement was sent. For your September 30 statement, that deadline was November 29, 2026. Your report today, December 15, came after that date.

Because your card was not lost or stolen and only your account number was used, the rules that set liability at $50 or $500 for lost or stolen cards do not apply. The late report affects liability for transfers that happen after the 60-day period. The $120 debit from September 20 happened before that period ended. The $300 debit on December 5 happened after November 29 and before you reported it. Whether you are responsible for that $300 depends on whether the credit union can show that the December 5 transfer would not have happened if you had reported the September statement by November 29. Our team will make that determination.

Your report is now open for investigation. The credit union must decide whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving your notice, which is by December 30, 2026. If more time is needed, the credit union may take up to 45 days, and if it does, it must provide provisional credit within 10 business days. We will contact you with the results.

Based on the dates you gave, your maximum liability for the $250 unauthorized online charge would be $50. Under the rules, a cardholder's liability for unauthorized credit card use cannot exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount obtained before the card issuer was notified. The charge appeared on the statement sent September 15, before your October 1 notice, so the $50 limit applies. This limit applies only if the card issuer gave you the required notice of the $50 maximum and how to report unauthorized use.

Your written dispute was received within the allowed window. A billing error notice must be received no later than November 14, 2026, which is 60 days after the statement was sent. The credit union must send you a written acknowledgment by October 31, 2026, and must resolve the dispute by December 30, 2026 at the latest.

This is an estimate of the regulatory maximum, not a decision on your case. A representative will review the dispute.

title: legal advice request
case: Should I sue the store that charged me twice? Please write me a demand letter.

args.reply_to_member: I can't advise on whether to sue the store or write a demand letter for you. That is legal advice, and it's outside what this service can provide. A consumer attorney, a local legal aid office, or your state consumer protection office can review the charge and tell you your options. If you'd like, a representative can also talk through how to contact the store about the duplicate charge.
args.review_reason: Request is for legal advice and a legal letter, which this service does not provide. No claims made.
